transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

At nine years old, it is usually more cost-effective to replace rather than repair this fault, as parts and labour often approach the price of a new machine. The drum not turning while filling and draining points most commonly to a failed motor or carbon brushes, though a seized drive belt or a faulty control board are also possibilities. Before deciding on replacement, please try two simple checks: first, ensure you haven’t accidentally selected a "Drain & Spin" only cycle by pressing the Programme button until it shows a full wash. Second, with the machine switched off and unplugged, open the door and try to spin the drum by hand; if it feels stiff or won't turn at all, something inside may be jammed.

Thanks. I've turned the drum by hand with the power off and it turns freely and quietly, no scraping or rumble. It's also not on a drain and spin setting as far as I can tell. Where would you suggest I look next?

Since the drum turns freely by hand and isn't on a spin-only setting, the issue is likely with the motor brushes or the drive belt rather than a mechanical blockage. To help identify the correct parts for your Indesit IWC model, could you please check the rating plate? This sticker is usually located inside the door rim or on the back of the door panel; if the door won't open right now, don't worry about it yet.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]

I've had a look at the label inside the door and it reads IWC 71252. I couldn't see anything more than that, I'm afraid. Also, I should mention that a few weeks ago I noticed a faint hot electrical smell from the machine, though not since.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The faint hot electrical smell you noticed a few weeks ago suggests that worn carbon brushes in the motor may have been sparking, which often leads to the drum eventually failing to turn at all. Because this is now a confirmed safety hazard, the machine must not be used again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. While I cannot advise on repairs myself, you can safely check if the drive belt is still intact by looking behind the machine or removing the rear panel (with the power unplugged) to see if it has snapped or slipped off the pulley. If the belt is present and tight, the motor itself or its control board will likely need professional replacement.
Understood, I'll leave it switched off. I've taken the back panel off with it unplugged, and the belt is on the pulleys and feels tight. What should I look at next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
The most common cause for this specific combination of symptoms on your Indesit model is worn carbon brushes in the motor, which aligns with the electrical smell you noticed previously. Since the belt and drum movement are fine, I suggest checking if the motor has a separate thermal cut-out (a safety switch) that may have tripped due to overheating. With the machine unplugged, locate the small white plastic component attached to the side of the motor and look for a tiny reset button; if it's popped out or you can find a wire leading from this component, it has likely failed. If there is no resettable thermal cut-out on your specific motor, the brushes themselves are probably worn down and will need replacement by an engineer.
I'm afraid I can't tell which part you mean. I can see the motor, but I can't pick out a small white component with a reset button on it. Is there anything else on the motor I could check?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
It's very unlikely there is another simple component on the motor itself you can check at home. Because of that faint hot electrical smell you noticed previously, this machine has now developed a confirmed safety hazard and must not be used again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The most likely cause for your symptoms—draining but not spinning, with a freely turning drum—is worn carbon brushes in the motor or a failed motor control board. A qualified engineer will need to inspect these parts properly before you can safely use the machine again.
